 protected override async Task SendAsync(HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)\\n        {\\n            //Hack to bypass handler already configured exception\\n            var field = this.GetType().BaseType.GetField(\\u0026#34;_authorizedUris\\u0026#34;, BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.NonPublic);\\n            field.SetValue(this, null);\\n\\n            var authState = await authStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync();\\n\\n            if (authState.User.Identity.IsAuthenticated)\\n            {\\n                ConfigureHandler(new[]{config.GetValue(\\u0026#34;ServerUri\\u0026#34;)});\\n            }\\n            else\\n            {\\n                //Satisfy validation so that we can call api without needing to be logged in\\n                ConfigureHandler(new[]{navigation.BaseUri});\\n            }\\n\\n            return await base.SendAsync(request, cancellationToken);    \\n        }\\n [2026-08-26T21:28:02.692Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 6194b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":67187,\"title\":\"Add an additional hook in Blazor WASM in the remote authentication flow before the AccountClaimsPrincipalFactory runs\",\"body\":\"## Background and Motivation\\n\\nI am using Microsoft Entra to sign my users into an application. However, the database for my application contains the roles and permissions along with other important metadata that I need to make available at client-side to integrate with components like AuthorizeView and the Authorize attribute at page level, along with using things like user.IsInRole(\\u0026#34;someRole\\u0026#34;).\\n\\nWhen I log in, I need a hook somewhere in the lifecycle that represents a point in the authentication process where I have access to the authentication token or ID token from Entra that contains my user\\u0026#39;s object ID so that I can make a call to my API and download some metadata about that user, store it somewhere like in sessionStorage, and then when my custom AccountClaimsPrincipalFactory logic fires and creates the ClaimsPrincipal, it can read from that storage location and update the ClaimsPrincipal being built up accordingly.\\n\\nIt is far too fragile to make the API call in the AccountClaimsPrincipalFactory and I often run into race conditions where the ClaimsPrincipal returned is incomplete, so I have had to put in a bunch of plumbing and extra parts on application startup to work around this missing hook in the authentication lifecycle.\\n\\nThe specific callback parameter type is less important than the lifecycle guarantee. The important requirement is that the callback runs after remote authentication has succeeded and before the client authentication state is published / before `AccountClaimsPrincipalFactory.CreateUserAsync(...)` is called.\\n\\nThe desired invariant is that application code can perform an awaited post-authentication bootstrap step before the first client-side `ClaimsPrincipal` is published to the app.\\n\\nIn my scenario, `AccountClaimsPrincipalFactory` should remain a deterministic mapper. It should not be responsible for acquiring tokens, calling APIs, handling token-interaction redirects, or deciding whether an incomplete principal is acceptable.\\n\\nThe missing hook would allow an app to:\\n\\n1. Receive the authenticated remote account or enough token/account metadata to identify the user.\\n2. Perform an awaited bootstrap operation, such as calling an application API.\\n3. Persist bootstrap data in a client-side store.\\n4. Then allow `AccountClaimsPrincipalFactory` to build the principal from already-available data.\\n\\nThis would make role/claim integration with `AuthorizeView`, `[Authorize]`, and `ClaimsPrincipal.IsInRole(...)` reliable for applications where Entra authenticates the user but application roles/permissions come from an app database.\\n\\n## Proposed API\\n\\n```\\nnamespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Authentication;\\n\\npublic partial class RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore\\n{\\n+    [Parameter] public EventCallback OnBeforeBuildingClaimsPrincipal { get; set; }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n(Please pardon me if the name isn\\u0026#39;t so great)\\n\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67187\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"stephajn\",\"id\":45795759,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/stephajn\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/45795759?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"api-suggestion\",\"api-proposal\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-06-12T16:20:46Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-06-15T11:59:51Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

with debugging a blazor webassembly client so I cannot confirm this but I think this method is hitting one of the cases that throws an exception or the empty this:\\n![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/78807/100962376-34f2f600-34f2-11eb-95fd-d919674e3e8c.png)\\n\\nSo I am leaning to the former.\\n\\n### To Reproduce\\nYou can reproduce the minutes.\\n\\nJust click the \\u0026#34;Fetch Data\\u0026#34; component link. While permissions are being checked → show a loader.\\n2. After the check:\\n   - If access is granted → render the protected body content.\\n   - If access is denied → render a fragment with a message about missing rights.\\n\\nThis is similar to the built-in `[Authorize]` attribute for components and the `AuthorizeView` wrapper for static UI elements.  \\nI was able to implement an `AuthorizeView`-like wrapper, but creating an `Authorize`-like attribute proved problematic.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Issues Encountered\\n1. **Authorize Attribute Limitations**\\n   - Cannot render a custom fragment when access is denied (e.g., message with missing rights).\\n   - Cannot easily pass parameters such as a list of required permissions and a custom context model\\n```csharp\\npublic class SecurityContext \\n{\\n    public int? ProjectId { get; set; }\\n    public int? DepartmentId { get; set; }\\n}\\n```\\nThe problem is that SecurityContext in dynamicly set from url, but attribute can contains only static info. So it is not an option. \\n2. **Layout Approach**\\n   - Attempted to use multiple layouts to handle authorization states, but Blazor only supports a single layout per page.\\n\\n3. **Inheritance Approach**\\n   - Implemented a base component (`SecurityComponentBaseCore` + `SecurityComponentBase`) that handles loading, access checks, and error messages.\\n\\n### Example: `SecurityComponentBaseCore.razor`\\n```razor\\n@if (Loading)\\n{\\n    \\n        \\n    \\n}\\nelse if (HasAccess)\\n{\\n    @Body\\n}\\nelse\\n{\\n    @ErrorMessage\\n}\\n\\n@code {\\n    public virtual bool Loading { get; set; } = true;\\n    public virtual bool HasAccess { get; set; } = false;\\n    public virtual string ErrorMessage { get; set; } = string.Empty;\\n    private protected virtual RenderFragment Body =\\u0026gt; builder =\\u0026gt; { };\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Example: `SecurityComponentBase.cs`\\n```csharp\\npublic abstract class SecurityComponentBase : SecurityComponentBaseCore\\n{\\n    [Inject] protected ISecurityManager SecurityManager { get; set; } = default!;\\n    [Inject] protected ILogger Logger { get; set; } = default!;\\n\\n    protected virtual SecurityContext Context { get; } = new SecurityContext();\\n    protected virtual List RequiredPermissions { get; } = [];\\n\\n    private protected sealed override RenderFragment Body =\\u0026gt; BuildRenderTree;\\n    protected new virtual void BuildRenderTree(RenderTreeBuilder builder) { }\\n\\n    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()\\n    {\\n        try\\n        {\\n            Loading = true;\\n            var res = await SecurityManager.HasAccess(Context, RequiredPermissions);\\n\\n            HasAccess = res.IsSuccess;\\n            Loading = false;\\n            if (!HasAccess)\\n            {\\n                ErrorMessage = res.ErrorMessage ?? \\u0026#34;Access denied\\u0026#34;;\\n            }\\n        }\\n        catch (Exception ex)\\n        {\\n            Logger.LogError(ex, \\u0026#34;Error checking permissions\\u0026#34;);\\n            HasAccess = false;\\n            ErrorMessage = \\u0026#34;Error checking permissions\\u0026#34;;\\n        }\\n        finally\\n        {\\n            Loading = false;\\n        }\\n    }\\n}\\n```\\n### Example: `MyComponent.razor`\\n```razor\\n@inherits SecurityComponentBase\\n\\n\\n    content\\n\\n\\n@code {\\n    protected override List RequiredPermissions { get; } = [\\u0026#34;right1\\u0026#34;, \\u0026#34;right2\\u0026#34;];\\n    protected override SecurityContext Context { get; } = new SecurityContext { ProjectId = 1 };\\n\\n    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()\\n    {\\n        await base.OnInitializedAsync();\\n        // Secure work here\\n        await Task.Delay(5000);\\n    }\\n}\\n```\\nThe problem in this scenario is that calling `StateHasChanged()` anywhere results in:\\n```\\nSystem.NullReferenceException: \\u0026#39;Object reference not set to an instance of an object.\\u0026#39;\\n```\\n\\nThis prevents showing the loader only during permission checks (instead it persists until the entire `OnInitializedAsync` of the derived component finishes and a 5‑second delay allows this to be shown). The call to `StateHasChanged()` is necessary in this scenario because it should trigger a re‑render: once the permission check completes, the component should update its UI so that the loader is replaced by either the protected content or the denied fragment. Without this re‑render, the loader remains visible longer than intended.\\n\\n---\\n\\n\\n# Question\\n\\nIs there a proper Blazor solution that allows building an `Authorize`-like mechanism with:\\n\\n- A loader displayed during the permission check  \\n- A custom denied fragment that shows missing rights  \\n- The ability to pass both a list of required permissions and a context model (`SecurityContext`)  \\n\\nIs there a recommended pattern or framework support for this scenario?  \\nAlternatively, could the existing `Authorize` attribute be extended or modified to handle these requirements?\\n\\nAttempting to implement something that was not originally intended feels fragile, especially since Blazor evolves quickly and such a workaround may stop functioning in future versions (I have already experienced this).  \\n\\nTherefore, the core question is: **Is there a proper, supported way to create an equivalent of `Authorize` or a reworked version that will reliably function in Blazor?**\\n\\nIt is possible that I have not fully understood all aspects of Blazor’s authorization system and may be missing something important. I would be glad to read any comments, clarifications, or suggestions.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/65007\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"mikermnv\",\"id\":109814953,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/mikermnv\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/109814953?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"investigate\",\"area-blazor\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":5,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":2,\"+1\":2,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-01-11T12:24:36Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-01-14T12:53:35Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

This is something we might want to consider improving by some sort of pinging mechanism to one of Identity\\u0026#39;s urls (like Account/Manage) via a fetch request using JS interop.\\n\\nThe other major challenge here is with regards to how AuthenticationService interoperates with other parts of the user app, like scoped services in their own \\u0026#34;sub-scope\\u0026#34;. This is relevant when users are leveraging things like Entity Framework for which we recommend using owning component scope as well as other libraries like HttpClientFactory that create their own scopes. In these cases, users are not able to access the current authenticated user within those services or any information associated with the circuit. The challenge here involves \\u0026#34;being able\\u0026#34; to have a \\u0026#34;per circuit\\u0026#34; scope that flows to any \\u0026#34;nested scope\\u0026#34;.\\n\\nThe other piece of feedback we\\u0026#39;ve received in this area involves how to communicate information to a given circuit from outside of the context of the circuit. This involves passing information during \\u0026#34;circuit\\u0026#34; startup and while the circuit is running. (it is triggered by the `@attribute [Authorize(Policy = \\u0026#34;Root\\u0026#34;)]` on the razor page)\\n\\nWhen a client lose connection with the server, the overlay `Attempting to reconnect to the server: N of M` appears:\\n\\n![image](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/22667054/3bc90594-35bc-4c18-b38e-36d049c2c170)\\n\\nWhen the client gains back the connection with the server, the same `Circuit` is maintained successfully and the authorization is validated again.\\n\\nWhen the process of the `IAuthorizationHandler` is very fast, the component will resume with its state successfully: \\n\\n![msedge_qx0mIIpW8p](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/22667054/725966b5-9cdc-4a73-ad34-4b031bb413b7)\\n\\nWhen the process of the `IAuthorizationHandler` is taking too \\u0026#34;long\\u0026#34;, the component will be unloaded, replaced with `Authorizing...` when reconnecting, then after authorization is successful, the component will be reloaded with a brand new state, which leads to losing the data that was on the page before losing connection with the server.\\n\\n![msedge_HSVumEpB7Y](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/22667054/25800601-c24c-4058-b5da-76ac325434dd)\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nIn my opinion, there is multiple expected behavior:\\n\\n- The `Authorizing...` should appear but the other component should keep its state while it is pending for authorization.\\n- The user should be able to prevent the `Authorizing...` from appearing. I configured the MSAL cache to use localStorage by setting the CacheLocation in MsalProviderOptions like this:\\n\\n```\\nbuilder.Services.AddMsalAuthentication(options =\\u0026gt;\\n{\\n    options.ProviderOptions.Cache.CacheLocation = \\u0026#34;localStorage\\u0026#34;;\\n    // other config...\\n});\\n```\\n\\nThis works well initially—tokens are stored and retrieved as expected. However, after a few hours (presumably when the token expires), the app doesn\\u0026#39;t seem to automatically acquire a new token. Even when I try to sign out manually using:\\n\\n`await SignOutManager.SetSignOutState();`\\n\\n...any pages decorated with `[Authorize]` still redirect to the NotAuthorized view. The only workaround I’ve found is to manually clear localStorage in the browser, which obviously isn’t ideal.\\n\\nAny insights or suggestions would be greatly appreciated!\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe expected behavior when using localStorage as the cacheLocation in a Blazor WebAssembly app with MSAL should be:\\n\\n- **Persistent Token Storage**: Tokens (ID, access, and refresh) should persist across browser sessions as long as they are valid and not manually cleared, since localStorage is not cleared on tab or browser close.\\n- **Automatic Silent Token Renewal**: When an access token expires, MSAL should attempt to silently acquire a new token using the refresh token (if available and valid), without requiring user interaction.\\n- **Graceful Sign-Out**: Calling SignOutManager.SetSignOutState() should clear the authentication state and redirect the user appropriately. After sign-out, protected routes decorated with [Authorize] should redirect to the login page or a configured fallback, not remain stuck on a NotAuthorized view.\\n- **No Manual Storage Clearing Required**: Users should not need to manually clear localStorage to resolve expired token issues. The library should handle token lifecycle management internally.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n1. Run a Blazor wasm project with Microsoft.Authentication.WebAssembly.Msal\\n```\\nservices.AddMsalAuthentication(remoteAuthenticationOptions =\\u0026gt;\\n{\\n    remoteAuthenticationOptions.ProviderOptions.Cache.CacheLocation = \\u0026#34;localStorage\\u0026#34;;\\n    webAssemblyHostBuilder.Configuration.Bind(\\n        \\u0026#34;AzureAd\\u0026#34;,\\n        remoteAuthenticationOptions.ProviderOptions.Authentication\\n    );\\n});\\n```\\n\\n2. appsettings.json with `AzureAd` section:\\n```\\n\\u0026#34;AzureAd\\u0026#34;: {\\n  \\u0026#34;Authority\\u0026#34;: \\u0026#34;Your-Authority\\u0026#34;,\\n  \\u0026#34;ClientId\\u0026#34;: \\u0026#34;Your-ClientId\\u0026#34;,\\n  \\u0026#34;ValidateAuthority\\u0026#34;: true\\n}\\n```\\n\\n3. Login into the project and wait until the token is expired.\\n4. Go back to the page and you\\u0026#39;ll not be able to navigate through the page. Token has not been correctly refreshed.\\n\\nNeed to manually clean localStorage to force app to get a new token.\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n9.0.204\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/61960\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"galehost\",\"id\":138874295,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/galehost\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/138874295?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"investigate\",\"area-auth\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":1,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":2,\"+1\":2,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-05-16T10:10:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-03T12:01:44Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

The page renders its static markup, `blazor` initialises, and\\nthen the runtime dies at startup with:\\n\\n```\\nError: AggregateException_ctor_DefaultMessage (Failed to fetch dynamically imported module:\\nhttp://127.0.0.1:5300/_framework/resource-collection.ty4X_.js)\\nTypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: .../_framework/resource-collection.ty4X_.js\\n    at un (.../_framework/dotnet.runtime..js)\\n    at rn.resolve_or_reject (.../_framework/dotnet.runtime..js)\\n    ...\\n    at .../_framework/dotnet.native..wasm:wasm-function[298]\\n```\\n\\nNothing is rendered by any `InteractiveWebAssembly` component; the page sits on its static content.\\n\\n**It is load-dependent, not random.** With one browser at a time it does not occur at all. With eight\\nconcurrent browsers it affects roughly half of page loads.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe runtime starts on every load. Concurrency between independent browser instances should not affect\\nwhether an app boots.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n**Repro: https://github.com/Memphizzz/BlazorBootBugRepro**\\n\\n```bash\\ngit clone https://github.com/Memphizzz/BlazorBootBugRepro\\ncd BlazorBootBugRepro \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; ./repro.sh\\n```\\n\\nStock template, stock Chrome, no test framework and no third-party packages. The **only** addition to\\nthe template is a component rendered with `prerender: false`, so the marker it renders can come from\\nnowhere but a started runtime. The repo is the output of:\\n\\n```bash\\ndotnet new blazor -o BootRepro --interactivity WebAssembly --empty\\n```\\n\\n`BootRepro.Client/Booted.razor`:\\n\\n```razor\\n\\u003cp\\u003eWASM-BOOTED\\u003c/p\\u003e\\n```\\n\\nappended to `BootRepro/Components/Pages/Home.razor`:\\n\\n```razor\\n\\n```\\n\\nThen run N headless Chrome instances at the same URL, each with a fresh profile, and count the DOMs\\nthat do not contain the marker:\\n\\n```bash\\nfor i in $(seq 1 8); do\\n  google-chrome --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-first-run \\\\\\n    --user-data-dir=\\u0026#34;$(mktemp -d)\\u0026#34; --virtual-time-budget=20000 \\\\\\n    --dump-dom \\u0026#34;http://127.0.0.1:5299/\\u0026#34; \\u0026gt; out-$i.html 2\\u0026gt;/dev/null \\u0026amp;\\ndone\\nwait\\ngrep -L wasm-booted out-*.html      # every file listed never started the runtime\\n```\\n\\n**Measured on the stock template above** (.NET 10.0.111, Chrome 143, Ubuntu 26.04):\\n\\n| concurrency | page loads | never started the runtime |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| **1 at a time** | 8 | **0** |\\n| **8 at a time** | 48 | **25** |\\n\\nThe serial arm is the control: same app, same browser, same budget, same marker — only concurrency\\ndiffers, so this is not the dump being taken too early.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n```\\nTypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module:\\n  /_framework/resource-collection..js\\n```\\nsurfaced as `AggregateException_ctor_DefaultMessage` from `dotnet.runtime..js`. It reaches\\n`console.error` only — it raises no `error` or `unhandledrejection` event, so a page-level error hook\\nsees nothing.\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.111\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n**ASP.NET Core**: 10.0.11 · **Chrome**: 143.0.7499.109 · **OS**: Ubuntu 26.04 (x64), WSL2 ·\\nno IDE (CLI).\\n\\n**Additional evidence from a private harness, offered because it narrows the mechanism.** The same\\nfailure occurs there, and a Chrome net-log (`--log-net-log`) of a failing browser shows:\\n\\n- **No `URLRequest` is issued for that module on the failing load** — not an error, not a hang: no\\n  request. The bytes never being asked for is the finding, and it is why raising client timeouts\\n  changes nothing.\\n- Across **1,522** `_framework` requests in that browser: **zero** ended with a `net_error` and\\n  **zero** never completed.\\n- When the module *is* requested it is served correctly — `200`, `Content-Type: application/javascript`,\\n  gzip, full length — so this is not the server, the MIME type, or the fingerprint.\\n- A per-load table across three non-victim browsers: **22 of 22** first-of-test loads fetched the\\n  module, no exceptions. A failing load is the one that did not ask for it.\\n\\n**Note on the resource**: `resource-collection.{fingerprint}.js` does not exist on disk; it is\\ngenerated and served by middleware (see #62249). We have not established whether that is relevant.\\n\\n**Why this repo**: the failing import is of a Blazor asset produced by the ASP.NET Core static-asset /\\nimport-map machinery, and the repro is a Blazor template — so `aspnetcore`. The stack, however, is\\ninside `dotnet.runtime.js` and `dotnet.native.wasm`, so if the defect is in the runtime\\u0026#39;s startup\\nimport path this belongs in `dotnet/runtime` and we would expect a transfer rather than a close.\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68697\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"Memphizzz\",\"id\":4660924,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/Memphizzz\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/4660924?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"Needs: Attention :wave:\"],\"comments\":3,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":1},\"created_at\":\"2026-08-21T16:31:27Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-25T13:23:46Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

[2026-08-26T21:28:22.453Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 7722b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":67980,\"title\":\"Blazor Web: exception during WASM root component activation is silently discarded — InteractiveAuto page stays a dead prerender with no error and no Server fallback\",\"body\":\"### Is there an existing issue for this?\\n\\n- [x] I have searched the existing issues\\n\\n### Describe the bug\\n\\n`WebAssemblyRenderer.OnUpdateRootComponents` fire-and-forgets the root component activation tasks:\\n\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/release/10.0/src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly/src/Rendering/WebAssemblyRenderer.cs#L72-L84\\n\\n```csharp\\ncase RootComponentOperationType.Add:\\n    _ = webRootComponentManager.AddRootComponentAsync(...);\\ncase RootComponentOperationType.Update:\\n    _ = webRootComponentManager.UpdateRootComponentAsync(...);\\n```\\n\\nIf activation throws (component constructor, DI resolution, a type-initializer failure in a dependency that only fails under Mono WASM, …), the fault is completely swallowed:\\n\\n- nothing in the browser console (no unhandled rejection, no `Blazor` error),\\n- no `blazor-error-ui`,\\n- no `ILogger` output,\\n- and for `InteractiveAuto`, **no fallback to Server**, even though the Server registration of the same page works (prerendering proves it).\\n\\nThe user is left on a permanently dead prerender. Worse: once Auto has committed to WebAssembly (runtime cached), even a **full page reload** of the affected page re-attempts WASM activation and dies the same way — there is no user-side recovery short of clearing the cache.\\n\\n**Real-world impact:** we hit this in production when a `TypeInitializationException` was thrown while constructing a ctor-injected DI service during activation of an `InteractiveAuto` page — but any exception thrown during activation triggers it; the specific trigger is irrelevant. Because the fault is discarded, diagnosing the underlying application-side bug took a multi-day investigation across CI bisects and Playwright traces, and ultimately required attaching an `AppDomain.FirstChanceException` handler in the WASM client — that handler is the only place the exception is observable. With ordinary error surfacing, the root cause would have been visible in the first failing run\\u0026#39;s browser console.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nSome combination of:\\n\\n1. The activation fault is logged (console + `ILogger`) and surfaces `blazor-error-ui`, like unhandled exceptions elsewhere in Blazor.\\n2. For `InteractiveAuto`, a failed WebAssembly activation falls back to the Server render mode instead of leaving a dead prerender (the server was able to render the page seconds earlier).\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\nMinimal repro (unmodified `dotnet new blazor -int Auto` template plus only the changes listed in its README): https://github.com/alexaka1/repro-dotnet--aspnetcore-wasm-silent-activation\\n\\nA service is registered working on the server and with a throwing factory in the WASM client:\\n\\n```csharp\\n// Client Program.cs — simulates a dependency that only fails on the WASM runtime\\nbuilder.Services.AddSingleton(_ =\\u0026gt;\\n    throw new InvalidOperationException(\\u0026#34;Simulated: service construction fails on the WebAssembly runtime.\\u0026#34;));\\n```\\n\\n1. `dotnet run`, open `/counter` — first interactive visit renders Interactive **Server**.\\n2. Navigate Home ↔ Counter until Counter reports **WebAssembly** (Auto committed to WASM).\\n3. Click the nav link to `/crash` (enhanced navigation), a page that injects the service.\\n4. Observe: page reports `RendererInfo: Static, IsInteractive: false` forever; button does nothing; browser console and server logs are clean. A `FirstChanceException` hook is the only evidence of the `InvalidOperationException`.\\n5. Full reload of `/crash`: same dead result (Auto stays on WASM once cached).\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\nOnly observable via `AppDomain.CurrentDomain.FirstChanceException`:\\n`System.InvalidOperationException: Simulated: service construction fails on the WebAssembly runtime.`\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.302\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n- ASP.NET Core version: 10.0.10 (behavior also reproduced on 10.0.9).\\n- Existing-issue search: `AddRootComponentAsync`, `OnUpdateRootComponents`, \\u0026#34;auto mode fallback\\u0026#34;, \\u0026#34;interactive auto stuck static\\u0026#34; — closest is #64508 ([Blazor] Unify root components initialization paths), which covers the divergent init paths but not the swallowed activation fault or the missing fallback.\\n- The same silent-discard exists for the `Update` operation.\\n- Happy to contribute a fix if you can indicate the preferred direction (await + log + error UI, vs. propagating the fault to enable Auto fallback).\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67980\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"alexaka1\",\"id\":22166651,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/alexaka1\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/22166651?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-07-23T14:16:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T07:22:48Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

For example:\\n\\n50 / 50 = 100%\\n50 / 51 = 98%\\n\\nThis results in the visible progress changing from 100% back to 98%, which\\nlooks broken and unprofessional to users.\\n\\nExpected behavior:\\n\\n- The total number of startup resources should be fixed before progress is reported.\\n- Progress must never decrease.\\n- 100% must only be reported after all required startup resources are loaded.\\n- Ideally, progress should represent downloaded bytes instead of only a resource count.\\n\\nPlease treat this as a correctness bug in the built-in Blazor loading indicator,\\nnot only as a feature request.\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe built-in Blazor WebAssembly loading progress must be monotonic.\\n\\nOnce the progress reaches 100%, it must never decrease again. The value 100% should only be reported after all startup resources have been discovered and loaded.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n    \\n    \\n    \\n\\n    \\n\\n\\n    \\n        \\u003cp\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\n    \\n\\n    \\n\\n    \\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n1. Create a standard Blazor WebAssembly application.\\n2. Replace the contents of wwwroot/index.html with the code above.\\n3. Publish and serve the application.\\n4. Open the browser developer console.\\n5. Reload the page.\\n\\nThe observer records all changes to Blazor\\u0026#39;s\\n--blazor-load-percentage CSS variable.\\n\\nOn the affected production application, the observed sequence included:\\n\\n87.74% -\\u0026gt; 100% -\\u0026gt; 96.30% -\\u0026gt; 99.38% -\\u0026gt; 100%\\n\\nThe browser console reports \\u0026#34;Progress decreased\\u0026#34; when the value moves\\nbackwards after already reaching 100%.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\nNETCoreApp,Version=v10.0\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n    \\u0026#34;name\\u0026#34;: \\u0026#34;.NETCoreApp,Version=v10.0\\u0026#34;,\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67979\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"RoellinRacing\",\"id\":154523119,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/RoellinRacing\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/154523119?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":1,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-07-23T12:16:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T06:27:27Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Try to authentication/logout endpoint.\\n\\n**Additional context**\\n\\n- DOTNET 10\\n- Template: https://github.com/dotnet/blazor-samples/tree/main/10.0/BlazorWebAppOidcBffAuto\\n\\nIs InteractiveWebAssembly not supported with the sample codes, or there any different changes we need to do?\\n\\n(cc: @guardrex https://github.com/dotnet/blazor-samples/issues/642)\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/65368\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"Schoof-T\",\"id\":2319986,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/Schoof-T\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/2319986?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-auth\",\"Needs: Attention :wave:\",\"Needs: Repro\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-02-09T12:00:32Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-19T07:44:43Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

The .NET/JS interop can continue using shared memory if we find it\\u0026#39;s necessary to have good perf on those older browsers (and thread safety is not difficult because it\\u0026#39;s all synchronous).\\n * **In a web worker (background thread) on more up-to-date browsers**. The .NET/JS interop will need to work by serializing any data that is being transferred rather than passing pointers [1].\\n\\nThis will be advantageous because then, even if your .NET code does something that locks up the CPU (such as a GC cycle), the UI will remain perfectly smooth (e.g., during animations or scrolling, or while the user is typing quickly into a textbox).\\n\\nThe existing UI update mechanism is designed around transferring batches of minimal diffs from .NET to JS, so it shouldn\\u0026#39;t be hugely difficult to have it express those diffs as serialized data rather than pointers into the WASM memory space. We\\u0026#39;ll have to be careful around things like event handling to ensure that the asynchrony can\\u0026#39;t result in inconsistency of behaviour versus the synchronous single-threaded model. For example, we will need to force all event delivery to be async as far as the JS side is concerned, even in the non-worker-thread case.\\n\\n*[1] Strictly speaking, we could also do it with shared memory on even newer browsers that support SharedArrayBuffer. But if we can get satisfactory perf without this, it would be better to serialize because it would mean fewer combinations of browser scenarios, and saves us having to deal with potentially complex thread-safety concerns on the .NET side.*\",\"state\":\"open\",\"state_reason\":\"reopened\",\"locked\":true,\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/5475\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"severity-minor\",\"affected-very-few\",\"not-on-roadmap\"],\"assignees\":[\"pavelsavara\"],\"milestone\":\".NET 12 Planning\",\"comments\":14,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":22,\"+1\":21,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":1,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2018-02-19T17:05:36Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-07-22T12:05:29Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":1,\"references\":[{\"number\":67768,\"title\":\"Run Blazor WebAssembly in a Web Worker\",\"state\":\"CLOSED\",\"url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67768\",\"repository\":\"dotnet/aspnetcore\"}]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

When navigating to `/error`, the Error page is rendered statically on the server, then when the client app starts, overwrites the Error page with the NotFound page content on the client. \\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe default project should demonstrate how to mix server-rendered and client-rendered content properly in the same app. Currently, the default project itself demonstrates mixing the render modes incorrectly.\\n\\nWhile putting `@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]` can be considered a workaround, it is undesirable: the layout of the application itself might still be using WebAssembly for even simple interactivity, like collapsing menus. `ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting` bypasses starting the WebAssembly runtime altogether.\\n\\nPossible solutions:\\n- Mark server-rendered content to persist on the client after client interactive routing kicks in. Possibly a marker attribute on the element, a directive, or an `@attribute` similar to `ExcludeFromInteractiveRoutingAttribute`.\\n- Allow `ExcludeFromInteractiveRoutingAttribute` to actually initialize the WebAssembly app, but leave the components marked with this attribute as-is in the DOM. Consider renaming the attribute if so. This might be easy to do using similar mechanics as seen in `PersistentState`\\n- Allow customizing the `Router`. For example, allow a behavior that lets the router \\u0026#34;keep\\u0026#34; the content as-is when a navigation event occurs, by overriding/passing `OnNavigatingAsync` or similar, or by inheriting from the built-in `Router`.\\n- Allow supplying a custom `Router` altogether. This would also allow multiple additional scenarios if community-built routers were to show up: handling localization in the URL, multiple hierarchic routers, etc.\\n- Allow rendering content on the server and let the client WebAssembly app \\u0026#34;consume\\u0026#34; the rendered static HTML as interactive. This might be a stretch, but for some simple cases, it can work.\\n- Modify/implement a new `RenderMode` that allows server-client handoff.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n`dotnet new blazor --name BlazorSSRCSR --all-interactive --interactivity WebAssembly`\\n`cd BlazorSSRCSR`\\n`dotnet run`\\n\\nNavigate to the created app\\u0026#39;s `/error` endpoint. The endpoint will show the server side error, then after a short time, the client side router overwrites the content with the client side `NotFound` page content.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.100-rc.1.25451.107\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\nThis is NOT the same as similar (possibly slightly related) issues:\\n- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/38128\\n- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/42561\\n\\nNote that there\\u0026#39;s also the implication that if this is done, \\u0026#34;mixing\\u0026#34; render modes across a hierarchy might become possible. Please describe the problem.\\n\\nWe currently have a not-so-streamlined option (`PersistentComponentState`) to preserve the state between SSR and Server/WASM. For example, if a page\\u0026#39;s data is fetched from the database in the host, the host sends the data to the client WASM so it won\\u0026#39;t be queried again.\\n\\nAs of my knowledge, in a normal Blazor page with Render Mode set to Auto and SSR enabled, the server always sends the SSR, then, according to the conditions, decides whether the client should establish a WebSocket connection, or use the WASM to fire up the client-side interactivity. WASM is large, so first users\\u0026#39; visits are mostly just WebSocket connections, which is not ideal, both for the user and the server. It introduces server overhead and delays all kinds of interaction for the user. But it\\u0026#39;s still better than waiting for the WASM to load, which might take a long time, depending on the project size.\\n\\n### Describe the solution you\\u0026#39;d like\\n\\nWhen we can share the state between SSR and WASM, why not try doing the same thing with WS/WASM? The page starts with SSR, and then, if WASM wasn\\u0026#39;t cached or outdated, fire up a WS connection. When WASM is loaded, immediately share the state with it and leave the control of DOM to WASM without refreshing the page.\\n\\nI think that if this gets implemented correctly, the overall user experience can be comparable to JS-based front-end frameworks.\\n\\n### Additional context\\n\\n_No response_\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/59641\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"1matin\",\"id\":70327745,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/1matin\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/70327745?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":3,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":9,\"+1\":6,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":3},\"created_at\":\"2024-12-26T08:17:01Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-01-08T17:13:45Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

Action { get; set; }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe login should complete without any errors and the user should be authorized.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\nI analysed the **AuthenticationService.js** file and the **RemoteAuthenticationService** class and debugged them step by step.\\n\\nWhat I\\u0026#39;ve noticed is that **CompleteSignInAsync** \\n```csharp\\nvar result = await JsRuntime.InvokeAsync\\u0026gt;(\\u0026#34;AuthenticationService.completeSignIn\\u0026#34;, context.Url);\\n```\\nreturns null - although in the browser storage i can see MSAL entries.\\n\\nI modified the AuthenticationService.js and mocked the completeSignIn method like this:\\n```js\\nasync completeSignIn() {\\n            console.warn(\\u0026#34;SIGN IN MOCKED!\\u0026#34;);\\n\\n            return {\\n                status: \\u0026#34;success\\u0026#34;,\\n                state: {\\n                    returnUrl: \\u0026#34;http://localhost:5175/\\u0026#34;\\n                }\\n            };\\n        }\\n```\\nI attached a logger to the **IJSRuntime InvokeAsync** methods  and noticed that when **CompleteSignIn** is called by the **RemoteAuthenticationService** it quickly returns null. But when I InvokeAsync the same method with the same parameters later in the code (by pressing a button for example), I\\u0026#39;m getting a correctly deserialized response.\\n\\nI added an arbitrary delay of 3s to any InvokeAsync calls of the **RemoteAuthenticationService**. Now suddenly all my issues are gone. **CompleteSignIn** return data. **GetUser()** returns a user also (which it didn\\u0026#39;t before) and all is well. This seems to be a race conditon. safeoutputs.description: WRITE-ONCE: do NOT call this tool with empty or placeholder arguments to probe or discover its schema — the required `body` field is listed in this schema; if you are not ready to post a real comment, call `noop` instead. Adds a comment to an existing GitHub issue, pull request, or discussion. Use this to provide feedback, answer questions, or add information to an existing conversation. For creating new items, use create_issue, create_discussion, or create_pull_request instead. IMPORTANT: Comments are subject to validation constraints enforced by the MCP server - maximum 65536 characters for the complete comment (including footer which is added automatically), 10 mentions (@username), and 50 links. Exceeding these limits will result in an immediate error with specific guidance. NOTE: Discussion comments are disabled for this workflow because discussions:write permission is not available. Set 'discussions: true' in the workflow's safe-outputs.add-comment configuration to enable discussion comments and request this permission. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 1 comment(s) can be added. Target: *. This tool records a real comment intent. Do not use it for placeholder comments, auth checks, or probing. Call it only when the final comment body is ready; otherwise use noop or report_incomplete.
safeoutputs.name: add_comment

safeoutputs.description: Add labels to an existing GitHub issue or pull request for categorization and filtering. Labels must already exist in the repository. For creating new issues with labels, use create_issue with the labels property instead. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 3 label(s) can be added. Only these labels are allowed: ["area-auth" "area-blazor" "area-commandlinetools" "area-dataprotection" "area-grpc" "area-healthchecks" "area-hosting" "area-identity" "area-infrastructure" "area-middleware" "area-minimal" "area-mvc" "area-networking" "area-perf" "area-routing" "area-security" "area-signalr" "area-ui-rendering" "area-unified-build" "by-design" "question" "external" "docs" "api-proposal" "test-failure" "performance"]. INTENT ENCOURAGED: Include rationale (string, max 280 chars) and confidence (exactly one of: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) with each call. These fields are optional but strongly encouraged — they improve transparency and should normally be included. Use suggest: true alongside rationale and confidence to route for human review.
safeoutputs.name: add_labels

safeoutputs.description: Remove labels from an existing GitHub issue or pull request. Silently skips labels that don't exist on the item. Use this to clean up labels or manage label lifecycles (e.g., removing 'needs-review' after review is complete). CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 1 label(s) can be removed. Only these labels can be removed: [needs-area-label].
safeoutputs.name: remove_labels

safeoutputs.description: Report that a tool or capability needed to complete the task is not available, or share any information you deem important about missing functionality or limitations. Use this when you cannot accomplish what was requested because the required functionality is missing or access is restricted. When a bash command is blocked by security policy, call this tool with reason set to "security".
safeoutputs.name: missing_tool

safeoutputs.description: Log a transparency message when no significant actions are needed. Use this to confirm workflow completion and provide visibility when analysis is complete but no changes or outputs are required (e.g., 'No issues found', 'All checks passed'). This ensures the workflow produces human-visible output even when no other actions are taken.
safeoutputs.name: noop

safeoutputs.description: Set the type of a GitHub issue. Pass an empty string "" to clear the issue type. Issue types must be configured in the repository or organization settings before they can be assigned. INTENT ENCOURAGED: Include rationale (string, max 280 chars) and confidence (exactly one of: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) with each call. These fields are optional but strongly encouraged — they improve transparency and should normally be included. Use suggest: true alongside rationale and confidence to route for human review.
safeoutputs.name: set_issue_type

safeoutputs.description: Report that data or information needed to complete the task is not available. Use this when you cannot accomplish what was requested because required data, context, or information is missing.
safeoutputs.name: missing_data

safeoutputs.description: Signal that the task could not be completed due to an infrastructure or tool failure (e.g., MCP server crash, missing authentication, inaccessible repository). Use this when required tools or data are unavailable and the task cannot be meaningfully performed. This is distinct from noop (no action needed) — it indicates an active failure that prevented the task from running. Provide a specific reason and optional details so downstream issue aggregation can preserve complete incomplete-signal context. The workflow framework will treat this as a failure signal even when the agent exits successfully.
